propositions: Rebar must support provider-native authentication chains and typed credential injection rather than implementing a universal secret broker or credential store, preserving SDK-owned refresh, rotation, and redaction semantics.
Static credentials (Jira, Jenkins, Gerrit API tokens) rotate only on process restart or redeploy; Rebar does not implement polling, hot-reload caches, or external secret manager retrieval.

Subprocess environments should inherit ambient variables and native credential helpers (Git, SSH, AWS) while removing only exact Rebar-declared sibling secret names and overlaying static values only for their owning child without mutating global os.environ.

Operation certificates accept exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (file) or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY (environment value); deployment resolves the source externally before startup and Rebar binds it context-locally without application-level SSM coupling.

Unavoidable static adapter credentials use Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes in non-serializable provider-specific containers, excluded from repr, comparison, hashing, snapshots, and logs; explicit unwrapping occurs only inside the sending adapter.

Current _bridge_runner propagates unrelated Jira/LLM/cloud credentials to reconciler children and ticket delivery; RP-04 must replace this with adapter-owned baseline environments and only selected auth capabilities per operation.
